overview.lead: Paladins heal, tank and fight in melee. Blizzard means Holy to be the strongest single-target healer and frames Retribution's group value around keeping Judgements up. Protection tanks with Righteous Fury, a taunting Seal of Fury and the Templar's Bulwark absorb.

Racials changed on 26 October: Human Ruthless is +1% crit and Dwarf Artisan's Precision is +1% hit with spells and attacks.

101.summary: What every Paladin should know before choosing a spec: the Forever changes, the class quests and the racial choice.

steps.text: Holy Strike arrives at level 6: an instant Holy-damage weapon strike on a 10 s cooldown.
Train Seal of Fury and Righteous Fury at level 10. Seal of Fury adds Holy damage to each swing plus an absorb worth half of it, and judging it taunts from 10 yards.
At level 20, Consecration and Blessing of Kings become baseline.
Judge freely: Judgement no longer consumes your Seal, so you never recast a Seal just to judge again.
Use Lay on Hands when it saves a life. Its cooldown is 20 minutes, not an hour.
Treat the beta reports of 5-minute Blessings, 1-hour Greater Blessings and a Divine Shield that halves your damage as unconfirmed: Blizzard's notes do not list them.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Salvation or Blessing of Light at the trainer.
mistakes.fix: Blizzard removed Salvation, Mass Salvation, Revoke and Blessing of Light.

mistakes.mistake: Planning a seal-twisting rotation.
mistakes.fix: Seal twisting is no longer baseline. Unsealed Wrath, a 31-point Retribution talent, takes the old Twist of Light capstone's place.

mistakes.mistake: Saving Lay on Hands as a once-an-hour button.
mistakes.fix: Its cooldown dropped from 1 hour to 20 minutes.

steps.text: At level 12, The Tome of Divinity grants Redemption.

At level 20, The Tome of Valor teaches Sense Undead and gives the Bastion of Stormwind shield. In The Test of Righteousness you gather materials in Deadmines, Shadowfang Keep, Loch Modan and Ashenvale, and Jordan Stilwell forges Verigan's Fist, a two-handed mace.
At level 40, ask your trainer about Summon Warhorse first: Warcraft Tavern lists it as a trainer unlock beside Apprentice Riding, while warcraft.wiki.gg links it to The Tome of Nobility.
Summon Charger (60) has no confirmed Forever quest yet. In Classic it came from a long chain from Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker that ended in Scholomance.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping the level 20 quests.
mistakes.fix: The Tome of Valor gives Sense Undead and the Bastion of Stormwind shield, and its follow-up rewards Verigan's Fist.

mistakes.mistake: Following a Classic guide for Summon Charger.
mistakes.fix: That chain is the Classic version; Warcraft Tavern lists the Forever quest as unknown.

overview.lead: Holy is the Paladin healer. Blizzard wants it to be the strongest single-target healer, viable in all group content, with group healing that needs planning.

points.text: Holy Shock heals an ally or hits an enemy on a 10 sec cooldown, and Light's Vigil at the bottom of the tree makes your next Holy Shock on its target heal their whole party.
Oath of Light strengthens your heals on one sworn ally, and Boundless Light raises Holy Shock's crit chance on everyone else.

101.summary: Leveling as Holy, the core healing rotation and the mana habits that matter first.

steps.text: Spiritual Focus now fills row 1. At 5/5 your Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil have a 70% chance not to lose casting time when you take damage.
Healing Light raises Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock healing by 12% at rank 3 of 3.
Take Divine Favor on row 3 on the way to Holy Shock on row 5.
Redemption comes from The Tome of Divinity, an Alliance quest at level 12.

mistakes.mistake: Saving a point for Consecration in the Holy tree.
mistakes.fix: Consecration is no longer a Holy talent; every Paladin learns it at level 20.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Improved Lay on Hands.
mistakes.fix: It is no longer in the Holy tree.

steps.text: Heal with Flash of Light and Holy Light. Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits cut 0.5 sec off your next Holy Light within 15 sec (Infusion of Light, rank 1).
Holy Shock is instant, reaches allies at 40 yd and has a 10 sec cooldown; keep it for targets whose health drops fast.
Place Light's Vigil on an ally for 30 sec. Your next Holy Shock on them has no cooldown and heals their whole party.
Use Divine Favor before a heal that must land big: it gives your next Flash of Light, Holy Light or Holy Shock a 100% critical effect chance, and Illumination returns mana after critical heals.
Swear Oath of Light on the ally who takes the most damage, usually the tank. Only one Oath of Light is active per Paladin.

mistakes.mistake: Casting Light's Vigil on an enemy.
mistakes.fix: Light's Vigil now targets friendly players only; its offensive effects were removed.

mistakes.mistake: Swearing Oath of Light on a second ally.
mistakes.fix: Only one Oath of Light may be sworn by the Paladin at any one time.

steps.text: Reverence at rank 2 of 2 lets 30% of your mana regeneration continue while you cast.
Spiritual Focus keeps Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil from losing casting time when you take damage.
Purifying Power cuts the mana cost of Cleanse and Purify by 20% at rank 2, which adds up in fights with a lot of dispelling.
Lay on Hands is on a 20-minute cooldown, so use it rather than hoard it.

mistakes.mistake: Hoarding Lay on Hands as an hourly button.
mistakes.fix: Its cooldown is now 20 minutes, down from 1 hour.

overview.lead: Protection is the Paladin tank. Righteous Fury raises all threat by 33% and adds a further 90% threat bonus to Holy damage, and judging Seal of Fury taunts from 10 yards.

points.text: Consecration does full damage only to the first 4 enemies, so it holds threat on about 4 targets.
Holy Shield moved to row 5 and leads to Shieldsworn, which makes Holy Strike trigger your shield talents and lets you block spells.

101.summary: Leveling as Protection, the core threat rotation and the cooldowns that keep you alive.

steps.text: Train Righteous Fury at level 10 and keep it on while you tank.
Redoubt gives melee attacks against you a 10% chance to raise your block chance, by 30% at rank 5 of 5, for 10 sec or 5 blocks.
Shield Specialization requires Redoubt. At rank 2 of 2 every block can restore 4% of your maximum Mana, at most once every 3 sec.
Templar's Bulwark is on row 3: an absorb equal to 100% of your maximum health for 8 sec.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Improved Seal of Fury or One-Handed Weapon Specialization.
mistakes.fix: Both were removed from the Protection tree.

mistakes.mistake: Planning on Blessing of Kings or Blessing of Sanctuary as Protection talents.
mistakes.fix: Blessing of Kings is baseline at level 20, and Blessing of Sanctuary is gone.

steps.text: Keep Righteous Fury on: it raises all threat by 33% and adds a further 90% threat bonus to Holy damage.
Keep Seal of Fury active and judge it to taunt from 10 yards. Judgement no longer uses up the Seal.
Use Consecration on packs. It does full damage only to the first 4 enemies, so pull in groups of about 4.
Use Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s). Iron Creed at rank 3 of 3 adds 30% threat to it and, while Righteous Fury is active, cuts your damage taken by 6% for 6 sec.
Keep Holy Shield up while melee hits are coming: 30% more block chance for 10 sec and 4 charges, with 75 Holy damage for each block.

mistakes.mistake: Recasting Seal of Fury after every Judgement.
mistakes.fix: Judgement no longer consumes your Seal.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting Consecration to hold a large pack.
mistakes.fix: It does full damage only to the first 4 enemies and very little to the rest.

steps.text: Save Templar's Bulwark for spikes. It has a 5 min cooldown, applies Forbearance for 1 min and cannot be cast while Forbearance is active.
Sacred Duty at rank 2 of 2 takes 60 sec off the cooldowns of Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark, and 10 sec off Forbearance.
Swift Judgement unleashes your Seal on a 1 min cooldown of its own and does not consume the Seal.
Improved Hammer of Justice takes 15 sec off Hammer of Justice's cooldown at rank 3 of 3.
Reckoning stores up to 4 extra attacks from blocks and crits taken and releases them on your next auto-attack.

mistakes.mistake: Planning two Templar's Bulwarks close together.
mistakes.fix: It has a 5 min cooldown and applies Forbearance for 1 min, and it cannot be cast while Forbearance is active.

overview.lead: Retribution is the Paladin melee damage spec. Blizzard frames its group value around keeping Judgements up on the target.

points.text: Unsealed Wrath is the 31-point talent and requires Repentance: melee hits store your active Seal for 15 seconds, up to three stacks, and a hit with a different Seal spends them.
Sacred Arbiter (row 4) adds 20% Holy Strike damage and makes Holy Strike refresh every Judgement on the target, including other Paladins'.

101.summary: Leveling as Retribution, the core rotation and the Seal habits that matter first.

steps.text: At level 20, The Test of Righteousness rewards Verigan's Fist, a two-handed mace. It suits Two-Handed Weapon Specialization: 6% more Physical and Holy damage at rank 3 of 3.
Conviction adds 6% crit with all spells and attacks at rank 3 of 3.
Seal of Command sits on row 3 of the Retribution tree.
Benediction cuts the Mana cost of all instant spells and abilities by 10% at rank 5 of 5.
Pursuit of Justice adds 8% movement and mounted speed at rank 1, but does not stack with other speed effects.

mistakes.mistake: Putting five points into Conviction.
mistakes.fix: Conviction has 3 ranks: 2%, 4% or 6% crit.

mistakes.mistake: Planning around Sanctity Aura or Improved Seal of the Crusader.
mistakes.fix: Neither is in the Retribution tree any more.

steps.text: Keep a Seal active, Seal of Command once you have it, and judge on cooldown. Judgement no longer consumes the Seal.
Use Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s). With Sacred Arbiter it deals 20% more damage and refreshes all Judgement effects on the target.
With Unsealed Wrath, let your melee hits store your active Seal (up to three stacks, for 15 seconds), then switch Seals and land a hit to spend the stacks.
Improved Judgement at rank 2 of 2 takes 2 sec off Judgement's cooldown.
Use Consecration when you need area damage. Holy Conduit, which lowers its mana cost, is a Holy talent now.

mistakes.mistake: Switching Seals before Unsealed Wrath has stored any stacks.
mistakes.fix: Stacks come from melee hits with your active Seal; a hit with a different Seal spends them.

mistakes.mistake: Letting Judgements drop on the target.
mistakes.fix: Holy Strike with Sacred Arbiter refreshes every Judgement on the target, other Paladins' included.

steps.text: Vindication gives your melee attacks a chance to lower the target's Attack Power by 68 for 30 sec at rank 1.
Eye for an Eye returns 5% of critical strike damage you take to the attacker at rank 1, capped at 50% of your total health.
Turn Evil lets Turn Undead affect Demons and, at rank 2 of 2, takes 1.0 sec off its cast time and 10 sec off its cooldown.
A Dwarf adds +1% hit with spells and attacks from Artisan's Precision.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting Vindication to raise your own Attack Power.

steps.text: Your raid value starts with Judgement uptime: Holy Strike with Sacred Arbiter refreshes every Judgement on the target.
Two-Handed Weapon Specialization now supplies Retribution's threat reduction, since Instrument of Law was removed.
In beta, Warcraft Tavern saw rank 7 of Blessing of Might give less attack power than in Classic, possibly a bug; check the tooltip.
In Classic, Retribution was brought mainly for its buffs; in Forever, Blizzard frames it around Judgements.

mistakes.mistake: Using the 16 October figure of 10/20/30% for Champion of the Light.
mistakes.fix: Blizzard's 2 Nov notes and the 10 November talent data give it five ranks, up to 60% of your Intellect at rank 5.

steps.text: Repentance incapacitates a Humanoid for up to 6 sec from 20 yd on a 1 min cooldown; any damage wakes the target.
Judging Seal of Command on a stunned or incapacitated target deals 137 to 145 Holy damage instead of 68 to 73.
Eye for an Eye at rank 2 of 2 returns 10% of the critical strike damage you take to the attacker.
Pursuit of Justice adds 15% movement speed at rank 2 of 2, but does not stack with other speed effects.
Against Hunters: Scorpid Sting now lowers your hit chance by 2%, and all traps share one 30-second cooldown and can be laid in combat.

mistakes.mistake: Hitting a target you just put in Repentance.
mistakes.fix: Any damage awakens the target, so use Repentance to take a Humanoid out of the fight for a moment, not as an opener.
